extracted.intended_audience: general readers, researchers, marketers, and social-media practitioners interested in internet culture and memes
extracted.subtask_description: An encyclopedic overview of defining traits, genres, propagation dynamics, social uses, and legal/marketing implications of internet memes; useful for analysing or creating memes and understanding what makes them spread or endure.

rubrics_metrics.name: Core characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Key characteristics of memes include their tendency to be parodied, their use of intertextuality, their viral dissemination, and their continual evolution.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This sentence frames the primary evaluative dimensions for memes: parodiability (can it be parodied?), intertextuality (does it reference other cultural texts?), virality (how easily does it spread?), and evolution (does it mutate / adapt over time?).

rubrics_metrics.name: Creative reproduction (mimicry vs remix)
rubrics_metrics.description: Creative reproduction refers to the adaptation and transformation of a meme through imitation or parody, either by reproducing the meme in a new context ("mimicry") or by remixing the original material ("remix").
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Mimicry example: different people recreate the viral video "Charlie Bit My Finger" in new contexts. Remix example: technological manipulation such as altering an image with Photoshop while retaining elements of the original. Evaluation: assess whether the reproduction preserves a recognisable core while adding novel context or form.

rubrics_metrics.name: Intertextuality
rubrics_metrics.description: Intertextuality in memes involves the blending of different cultural references or contexts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Example: combining Mitt Romney's phrase "binders full of women" with a frame from Psy's "Gangnam Style" to create new meaning. Assessment: degree to which a meme relies on or skillfully fuses distinct cultural texts to create humor or commentary.

rubrics_metrics.name: In-joke vs broad comprehensibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet memes can function as in-jokes within specific online communities, conveying insider knowledge and fostering collective identity, or they can achieve widespread cultural relevance understandable by broader audiences.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation should consider target audience: is the meme intended to signal group membership (high insider content) or to be widely legible and shareable across communities?

rubrics_metrics.name: Replicability (fidelity)
rubrics_metrics.description: Adaptation of Dawkins' 'fidelity' for internet memes is better described as replicability, since memes are frequently modified through remixing while still maintaining their core message.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a meme maintains a recognisable core through successive reproductions (high replicability) versus becoming unrecognisable.

rubrics_metrics.name: Fecundity (ability to spread)
rubrics_metrics.description: Fecundity, or the ability of a meme to spread, is promoted by factors such as humor, intertextuality, and the juxtaposition of seemingly incongruous elements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples cited: humor in "All your base are belong to us", intertextual pop-culture referencing in "Star Wars Kid" renditions, juxtaposition as in "Bert is Evil". Evaluation: measure how readily a meme is remixed/shared and which features (humor, familiarity, incongruity) contribute.

rubrics_metrics.name: Longevity
rubrics_metrics.description: Longevity is essential for a meme's continued circulation and evolution over time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether a meme endures beyond a fleeting spike — does it continue to be reused, remixed, or referenced across time and contexts?

rubrics_metrics.name: Evolution and propagation dynamics (SIR-like viral pattern)
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet memes propagate in a similar pattern to infectious disease (SIR model): an initial spike in popularity followed by a gradual taper to obscurity; memes can remain consistent or evolve, changing meaning or structure.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation can consider lifecycle stage (emergent, peak, fading) and the meme's capacity to evolve (meaning shifts, structural retention). The SIR analogy suggests tracking susceptible/exposed/infected/recovered dynamics.

rubrics_metrics.name: Format versatility
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet memes manifest in a variety of formats, including images, videos (e.g., GIFs), and other viral content; newer formats include short-form videos popularized by Vine and TikTok.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the meme format fits the platform and affordances (static image, GIF, short video), and how format influences spread, remixability, and reception.

rubrics_metrics.name: Dank meme features
rubrics_metrics.description: "Dank memes" are a genre referring to deliberately zany or odd memes with features such as oversaturated colors, compression artifacts, crude humor, strange captions, and overly loud sounds (termed 'ear rape').
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use these visual/auditory hallmarks to classify a meme as 'dank'; note that 'dank' may also mean an overused/stale meme that becomes funny again through irony.

rubrics_metrics.name: Deep-fried meme features
rubrics_metrics.description: "Deep-fried" memes refer to those that have been distorted and run through several filters and/or layers of lossy compression.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: the 'E' meme; evaluation: degree of visual/artifact degradation, saturation, and absurdity produced by successive reprocessing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Surreal meme characteristics
rubrics_metrics.description: Surreal memes make use of humorously absurd and even surrealist themes, often incorporating layers of irony and nonsensical elements as escapism from mainstream meme culture.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: "they did surgery on a grape" and the 'moth meme'. Evaluate on measures of absurdity, layered irony, and emotional/escapist function.

rubrics_metrics.name: Short-form video meme conventions
rubrics_metrics.description: Short-form video memes (originating with Vine and now common on TikTok) are often scripted sketches or short clips that circulate as meme formats.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess timing, punchline economy, repeatability (audio/video snippet reuse), and platform-specific affordances (loops, duet/remix features).

rubrics_metrics.name: Low-quality / 'brain rot' classification
rubrics_metrics.description: Newer internet memes (specifically those of low quality) are often classified as 'brain rot' or 'AI slop'; the term describes content lacking in quality and meaning, often associated with slang and trends popular among younger generations.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this label to flag memes that prioritize repetition/trend-chasing and opaque slang over coherent humor or meaningful content.

rubrics_metrics.name: Memetic marketing authenticity and fit
rubrics_metrics.description: Memes allow brands to circumvent the conception of advertisements as irksome by using existing memes or creating new ones, but forced, unoriginal, or unfunny usage can negatively impact brand image.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: Gucci reimagining popular memes; Wendy's faced criticism after sharing a controversial Pepe meme. Evaluation criteria for brand memes: authenticity, audience fit, timing, creativity, and risk of backlash.

rubrics_metrics.name: Political meme effectiveness and risk
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet memes are a medium for fast communication to large online audiences and can function like modern political cartoons; they can inform, influence turnout, damage reputations, or be commodified.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: the 'Dean scream', a meme that damaged Ted Cruz's campaign, and campaigns buying meme dissemination. Evaluate political memes on clarity of message, memetic spread, ethical implications, and susceptibility to misinterpretation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Social movement utility
rubrics_metrics.description: Internet memes can construct collective identity and provide platforms for discourse and mobilization, raising awareness or funds (e.g., It Gets Better Project, Ice Bucket Challenge).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess a meme's capacity to build solidarity, communicate a cause succinctly, and translate online engagement into offline outcomes (awareness, donations, turnout).

rubrics_metrics.name: Copyright / fair use considerations
rubrics_metrics.description: Because many memes derive from pre-existing works, they may implicate copyright; U.S. fair use analysis uses four factors: (1) purpose and character (transformative), (2) nature of the copyrighted work, (3) amount and substantiality used, and (4) effect on the market for the original.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate whether a meme is transformative (gives novel meaning or expression), uses limited portions, draws from factual sources (favours fair use), and is non-commercial (less likely to harm market). These factors guide legal risk assessment for creating/distributing memes.

rubrics_metrics.name: Community reinterpretation and creator reception
rubrics_metrics.description: As memes move through different communities, they are reinterpreted to suit those communities' needs, often diverging from the creator's original intent; mainstreaming can cause original creators to lose favour with the meme.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider origin-community norms and likely reactions to mainstream spread; evaluate sustainability of a meme's authenticity after cross-community adoption.

rubrics_metrics.name: Propagation vs longevity trade-offs
rubrics_metrics.description: Research suggests memes that experience exceptionally high peaks in popularity are unlikely to endure unless uniquely distinct, whereas memes without such peaks but that coexist with others tend to have greater longevity.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use this to evaluate memetic strategy: whether to aim for explosive virality (risking short life) or steady coexistence/remixability (potentially longer life).
